label: Front Range Hikes
description: 30 Colorado hikes — from alpine cathedrals to flat 'is this even a hike' walks.

items.name: Royal Arch
items.note: A steep grind under the Flatirons to a giant stone arch. Boulder's rite of passage.

items.name: Mount Sanitas
items.note: A lung-busting loop right off the edge of Boulder. Everyone's local benchmark.

items.name: Chautauqua Flatirons Loop
items.note: The postcard. The Flatirons rising straight out of the meadow.

items.name: Sky Pond
items.note: Past a waterfall you have to scramble up, to a lake ringed by spires. Worth every step.

items.name: Hanging Lake
items.note: A turquoise, travertine-fed lake so fragile you need a permit. Unreal in person.

items.name: The Manitou Incline
items.note: 2,700 steps, 2,000 feet up, in under a mile. A stairmaster designed by a villain.

items.name: Emerald Lake
items.note: Three gorgeous lakes on the way to a fourth. The most beloved easy hike in RMNP.

items.name: Mount Bierstadt
items.note: The 14er everyone climbs first. Bag a peak, then brag about it forever.

items.name: Devil's Head Lookout
items.note: Climb a staircase to a working fire lookout with a 100-mile view.

items.name: Saint Mary's Glacier
items.note: A short hike to a lake and a permanent snowfield. Bring a sled, unironically.

items.name: Chief Mountain
items.note: The biggest view-to-effort ratio on the Front Range.

items.name: Herman Gulch
items.note: Wildflowers in July, a lake at the top, and it's right off I-70.

items.name: Grays and Torreys Peaks
items.note: Two 14ers in one day. Overachiever energy.

items.name: Longs Peak (Keyhole Route)
items.note: A 15-hour, pre-dawn, occasionally terrifying epic. Type-two fun at its finest.

items.name: Quandary Peak
items.note: A great 14er that everyone and their mountain goat also picked today.

items.name: Mount Blue Sky (Mount Evans) Summit Lake
items.note: You can drive most of the way up, which purists find deeply offensive.

items.name: Apex Trail
items.note: Great trail, if you enjoy leaping out of the way of mountain bikers on odd days.

items.name: Red Rocks Amphitheatre Stairs
items.note: Not a hike. It's fitness bros doing bear crawls up the seats at 6am. Chaos.

items.name: Washington Park Loop
items.note: A pancake-flat city loop past two lakes. Calling it a 'hike' starts fights.

items.name: Cherry Creek Regional Trail
items.note: It's a paved bike path. You are not hiking. You are commuting with snacks.

items.name: Sloan's Lake Loop
items.note: Great skyline views, zero elevation gain, one very confident 'hiker.'
